scores.notes: The only plan that caught the decisive recipe fact. The chin Tracker.track pastes the whole raw 256x256 face into FaceMesh's frame (verified at experiments/chin_fps_validation_20260927/run.py:38-41, called at :139). So the 0.345 ms staged crop is not exact under 100% chin, and the measured-component path is about 287-299 fps, not 304.6. Its other checks also held up: power limit = max = 220 W; the backup engine is a different build; the ONNX bs16 factor comes from ONNX per-block ratios (1.025/0.807/0.946/1.069/0.866, which I re-derived); and the double-counting ledger. Weaknesses: it assumes 0.97 expected live efficiency, which is optimistic for a never-measured live path; its ONNX high case ignores that per-block timings started from 2790-2805 MHz idle clocks; and it gives less detail on process architecture, admission and startup RAM.

Best sequencing and measurement design. Strengths: a layered L1-L5 baseline with a null sink, redirect and kill rules, fresh fps taken from /webrtc/sessions/stats track counters, a clear target architecture with invariants (one CUDA-issuing thread, never wait on media, ordered per stream, run-ahead stored as faces), and a per-process budget. Its 300 fps path depends on the TAESD staged crop (0.345-0.403 ms) under the chin recipe, which is invalid because the tracker reads the full face. That makes its measured 304.6 ceiling and its P2-P3 rows wrong for the required recipe. Code references were accurate.

Strongest on the model: the stagewise ONNX backend as a single path for FP16 and INT8 (a monolithic INT8 Q/DQ export exceeds the 2 GB protobuf limit), the multi-avatar calibration corpus, the per-block sensitivity table, the recovery ladder, lossy gates L1-L8 with an FP16 noise floor, freeing the eager UNet from VRAM (verified at avatar_manager_parallel.py:170), and the note that TRT 10.9 on the box is runtime-only. Errors: it applies the torch_tensorrt bs16+graph factor 0.9055 to the ONNX path; it claims graph mode frees the spinning core, but gil.json shows 23.5 ms CPU per call still spinning; and it relies on the staged crop under chin. Its 75-80% confidence for 300 is therefore overstated.

Adds verified product and ops facts the others missed: the group cap of 12 (api_server.py:3539/3982) blocks a 15-20 tile wall test; the wall ran libx264 because native VP8 was not enabled; there is a 10.5 GB startup RSS transient; idle sessions alone exceed the event-loop ceiling; /tmp/torchinductor_root must be kept for SHA baselines; plus binomial and run-ahead burst math, admission via worker_control_plane, SLOs, and S0-S5 scenarios. It also relies on the staged crop (its P3.6 checks the chin warp, not the tracker). Its today-efficiency figure (0.53-0.56) is the contaminated observed number without the structural ceiling next to it. The process split comes late and is sized XL.

reviews.verdict: Most of the plan's arithmetic reproduces from the probes: the ms/frame figures, the per-block INT8/FP16 sums (16.30, 15.82), the TAESD 0.85/0.51 baselines, the binomial table, and the disk and engine sizes all check out. There is also no double counting between the CUDA-graph gain and the bs16+graph figure, or between the 0.739 and 0.86 TAESD baselines. The headline, though, is inflated by an efficiency factor that goes up from 0.93 to 0.95 when chin goes live, on the strength of a CPU-only synthetic load. With the plan's own P1/P2 efficiencies the expected case is about 314 fps (272–346), not 321 (285–350). On top of that, the go/no-go threshold of 2.62 ms does not deliver 300 at any efficiency below 0.955. The plan also ties the measured ONNX-path gain (measured at bs8) to an unmeasured bs16 factor, and misses that ONNX stagewise at bs8 alone roughly matches or beats the torch_tensorrt bs16 fallback. Several derivations are internally wrong: the pessimistic 2.62 ms, the "×0.953×0.984 = 2.78" line, the "6% sum-of-blocks overstatement", the row-2 delivered figures, and "Other" set at 0.05 when its own parts add to 0.08. Every "sustained" number comes from a run of about 60 batches (1.5–2 s), which breaks the plan's own R5 rule that only runs of 60 s or more count. The INT8 quality picture quotes the flattering full-frame metrics instead of the used-rows metrics its own gate uses, and it never says whether the repo gate G-UNET, which INT8 misses by about 5×, applies to 6.2. Verdict direction ("300 at the expected case, not the low case; 400 not lossless") survives, but with a thinner margin (~5%) and a stricter go criterion.

issues.claim: Expected: about 321 fps delivered, range 285–350 … 2.96 GPU-ms per frame → 338 fps ceiling × 0.95 live efficiency (P3/P4 efficiency 0.92/0.95/0.98, vs P1/P2 0.88/0.93/0.97)
issues.problem: Efficiency goes up when the CPU-heavy chin chain is added in-process. The plan's own §3 table has P2 (standard compose) delivering 273/314/346, then P3/P4 delivering 285/321/350 at the same GPU ms. The justification is C_chin15 and G (0 late frames), but that is a CPU-only synthetic load with no GPU scheduler thread, and P4 is only conditional at 15 streams. At 300 fps the in-process chin chain already takes about 45–53% of the per-process GIL ceiling (567–665 fps), and GIL contention was measured to grow torch_tensorrt enqueue from 4.5 to 14 ms. The low end also ignores the historical 3090 live/implied ratio of 0.80–0.85 and the plan's own K1 threshold of 0.85.
issues.correction: Keep P3/P4 efficiency at or below the P1/P2 values until in-server numbers exist. Expected ≈ 338×0.93 = 314 fps. Range 310×0.88 = 272 (263 at the K1 threshold of 0.85) up to 357×0.97 = 346. Margin over 300 is about 5%, not 7%. Row 3a likewise becomes 259–292, not 271–295. Say plainly that the 0.93 is an assumption with no live evidence: the only live figure is 0.53–0.56, contaminated.
issues.evidence: Plan §3 table rows 'After P2 … 273 / 314 / 346 (standard compose)' vs 'After P3/P4 … 285 / 321 / 350'. cpu_probe/results_combined.jsonl: C_chin15 is synthetic (chin_surrogate=3, no GPU) at 5.14 proc cores; U_ceiling_chin_pyav_8/16/32 at 665/623/567 fps. EVIDENCE_DIGEST: 'with other Python threads busy, enqueue grew 4.5 -> 14 ms'. wf1_result.json history reader: '3090 observed/implied ratio was about 0.80-0.85'. Arithmetic: 1000/2.96 = 337.8; ×0.93 = 314.2; 1000/3.23 = 309.6; ×0.88 = 272.4; ×0.85 = 263.2.

issues.claim: Go criterion: ≤2.62 ms per frame sustained, i.e. at least 6% better than 2.79. This number decides the 300 verdict.
issues.problem: A UNet at 2.62 ms gives 2.62+0.51+0.05 = 3.18 ms → 314 fps ceiling, so 300 needs 95.5% efficiency, above the plan's expected 0.93–0.95. The threshold also conflicts with the Phase 2 exit (≤3.0 ms per frame all-in, which means UNet ≤2.44 ms). A 2.45–2.62 ms result would pass 2.2 and then fail the P2 exit.
issues.correction: Derive the go threshold from the efficiency needed: UNet_max = 3.333·e − (TAESD + other). With 0.51 + 0.05: 2.37 ms at e=0.88, 2.44 at 0.90, 2.54 at 0.93, 2.61 at 0.95 (0.03 lower if 'other' is 0.08). Set 'go for 300 lossless' at ≤2.44–2.54 ms. Treat 2.54–2.62 as 'marginal: needs a 6.x backstop'. Match the P2 exit to the same number.

issues.claim: It needs the ONNX-parser bs16 FP16 UNet … K4: bs16 fails G-UNET twice: stay on bs8 (287 ceiling with TRT TAESD).
issues.problem: The ONNX-path gain was measured only at bs8: 20.575 ms per bs8 as a sum of 11 real per-block engines. The bs16 factor for that path is an extrapolation from 5 micro-blocks. Item 2.3 ships exactly this 11-block stagewise layout, so at bs8 the per-block sum is close to a direct measurement of the shipping configuration. The plan folds the ONNX path and bs16 into one lever, and its K4/K2 fallbacks drop the ONNX bs8 option.
issues.correction: Split the lever: 2.3a is ONNX stagewise at bs8 plus a CUDA graph, 2.3b is bs16 on top. ONNX bs8 is about 2.572 × 0.9825 (raw-TRT graph gain) = 2.53 ms → 3.09 ms total → 324 ceiling → about 301 at e=0.93 (313→291 with half the clock penalty). That is comparable to or better than the torch_tensorrt bs16 fallback (2.79 ms), at lower latency and gate risk. The 2.2 bench should measure both stagewise bs8 and bs16. K4 should fall back to ONNX bs8 (about 324 ceiling), not the .ts bs8 (287).
issues.evidence: unet_probe/trt_topblocks_bs8.json sum_fp16_ms = 20.575 (bs8 only; no bs16 top-block run exists). trt_raw (wf1_result unet measurements): raw TRT 24.04 → graph 23.62 ms (−1.75%). ttrt_bs16.json 44.63/16 = 2.79. Arithmetic: 20.575/8 × 0.9825 = 2.527; +0.56 = 3.087 → 324 fps.

issues.claim: §3.1 pessimistic '× 1.0 × 0.995 × 1.0 × ~1.04 → 2.62 ms'; Correction 3: '20.58 × 2790/2565 = 22.4 ms/bs8 → × 0.953 × 0.984 = 2.78 ms/frame ≈ the 2.79 fallback'; INT8 pessimistic uses × 1.088

Correction 3's own factors give 2.62, not 2.78; 2.78 needs bs16 factor 1.0 and graph 0.995 on top of the full clock penalty. So 'worst case ≈ no gain' is a stacked worst case, not what the text says. The FP16 pessimistic case uses half the clock penalty (1.04) while the INT8 pessimistic uses all of it (1.088), which softens the FP16 low case compared with INT8.

Low-case total becomes 2.67+0.53+0.08 = 3.28 ms → 305 ceiling → 268–281 delivered. Rewrite correction 3 as: expected factors plus full clock penalty = 2.62 ms (−6%); no bs16 gain plus full clock penalty = 2.78 ms (no gain).

issues.claim: Partly offsetting this: summing blocks overstated eager time by about 6% (39.46 ms sum vs 37.1 ms for the whole forward); sum-of-blocks correction 0.98 / 0.99 / 1.0

The same-session eager.json shows the per-block sum (37.35 ms) against the full forward (37.11 ms) is only 0.6%. A sum-of-blocks discount double-counts against the plan's own design choice.

issues.claim: The per-block timings also started from an idle, boosted GPU (idle samples 2790–2805 MHz [M trt_topblocks_bs8.json]). The shipping engine was measured sustained at 2520–2565 MHz [M p6].
issues.problem: The idle samples say nothing about clocks during the runs. gpu_state() syncs and sleeps 1.2 s before sampling, and the same function logged 2505 MHz idle for trt.json and ttrt_bs16 round0 and 2790 for p6's pre-sample. The real, unmeasured mechanism is burst length: per-block timing is sync-per-call with 30 calls of 0.03–4.8 ms, so average power stays low. Whole-UNet short runs (trt.json 24.62 ms, raw 24.04) were not slower than the 'sustained' p6 run (24.03), which suggests the penalty may be small. The 0–8.8% penalty is a hypothesis, not evidence.
issues.correction: Tag the clock penalty [I] with a range of 0–9%, and give the mechanism as burst duty cycle. Settle it cheaply first: rebuild the 11 FP16 per-block engines in RAM (184 s total build) and time them back-to-back as one chained forward for ≥60 s at the power cap, logging clocks. That is also the stagewise bs8 backend.
issues.evidence: unet_probe/common.py gpu_state(): 'torch.cuda.synchronize(); time.sleep(1.2)' before nvidia-smi. probe_trt_topblocks.py gpu_ms(): s.record(); fn(); e.record(); e.synchronize() per iteration. trt.json idle sample 2505 MHz; p6 'pre_UNet[default]' 2790 MHz, then 2565 under load.

issues.claim: Only sustained ≥60 s numbers count (R5); 23.43 ms 'sustained' [M p6]; 3a 'all components measured'
issues.problem: No ms figure in the plan comes from a run of 60 s or more. The p6 'sustained' configs are N=60 batches, about 1.5–1.9 s each (48 s total across 8 configs, GPU 40→66 °C). ttrt_bs16 is 2×(10+30) calls, and the TAESD figures are 50 iterations at 2775–2790 MHz. The full-height TRT TAESD with fused uint8 output, the one 2.1 ships, was never built: the 0.486 ms is FP16 NCHW output. So row 3a is not 'all measured', and the whole waterfall is exposed to an unmeasured thermal-soak drop, likely a few percent against a ~5% margin.
issues.correction: Label p6 as '60-batch power-capped burst (~1.5 s)', not sustained. Add a thermal-soak uncertainty of about +0–3% GPU ms [I] to every row until a ≥60 s run exists. Make the item 0.8 L1 null-sink run the first ≥5 min measurement of today's GPU path. Tag full-height u8 TAESD as [I] and give it a range of 0.50–0.55 (the compiled path's in-pipeline overhead was about 11%, the crop's 2–5%).

issues.claim: Where INT8 quality stands today: naive INT8 gives latent rel-L2 7.07% and PSNR 41.8 dB … SmoothQuant α sweep (the default only moved 7.07% → 6.75%)
issues.problem: The quoted metrics are full-frame, but the plan's own L2 gate is on used rows (mean ≥45 dB, worst ≥42). The probe's lower-half PSNR, the rows the blend uses, is 40.3 mean / 37.3 min, about 5 dB short on both. SmoothQuant made the used-row metric worse (39.9 / 35.9) even though rel-L2 improved, so presenting it as a small improvement and making it recovery step 2 misreads the data. The plan also leaves out that the best measured INT8 (conv-only, linears in FP16) is still 6.09%, about 16× the FP16 floor. And the evaluation is 64 frames of one avatar, calibrated on the same avatar, decoded with SD-VAE rather than the required TAESD.
issues.correction: Report INT8 as: used rows 40.3 dB mean / 37.3 dB min against a gate of ≥45 / ≥42; SmoothQuant worsens used rows; best PTQ variant 6.09% / 41.1 dB used rows; single avatar, SD-VAE decode. Rerun the accuracy probe with TAESD on held-out avatars before scheduling 6.2. Say that recipe v1's error is unmeasured and that per-block errors of 3–5% remain in the 7 INT8 blocks.

issues.claim: G-UNET applies to 2.3, 2.4, 6.2 (mae_max ≤0.01, max_abs ≤0.5) … each [6.1, 6.2] has roughly a 40% chance of passing your video review → 75% confidence
issues.problem: If G-UNET applies to 6.2, INT8 has to cut its error about 5× (inferred INT8 RMSE of about 0.059 against a 0.01 MAE gate), which PTQ recipes have not come close to (7.07% → 6.09% best). The table then says L1–L8 thresholds are D17, so the numeric bar for 6.2 is undefined. The 40% pass probability has no evidence behind it, and the 75% does not follow from it: two independent 40% backstops on a 40% failure mass give 0.60 + 0.40×(1−0.6²) = 0.86, or 0.76 for one. K3 also correlates 6.1 with TRT TAESD.
issues.correction: Pick one bar for 6.2: either G-UNET (which in practice means QAT or distillation) or the L-gates alone with the user's thresholds. Label the INT8 pass probability as unknown and low for PTQ-only, with QAT as the realistic path. Show the confidence arithmetic, or drop the percentages.

issues.claim: bs16 factor: 0.953 (expected; weighted ONNX per-block ratios [M])

reviews.verdict: Through the serving, CPU, RAM and VRAM lens, the plan does not support "300 yes at the expected case." The VRAM and NVENC handling is adequate. The GPU-side sequencing (2.2 bench before code) is sensible. The problem is the headline 321 fps: it multiplies a 338 fps ceiling by a live efficiency of 0.95 that has never been measured. Every live ratio on record is lower: 0.80-0.85 historically, 0.53-0.56 today. Hitting 300 needs at least 0.89. The 8.3 GB RAM budget cannot be traced to any source and leaves out most of the split's processes. Right now there is 11.95 GB available with no server running, and the plan's own "+4 GB" guard means no 15-stream run can happen without D2. That includes the decisive 2.2 bench. The claim that chin works in one process rests on a thread-only synthetic bench. That bench has no GPU feeder, no asyncio/aiortc, no tracker IPC and a lighter chin stand-in, and it already shows GIL convoying, so Phase 4 is probably needed for 300. The verdict should read "unproven: about 287 fps at the best historical live ratio." A saturating P1 run, a RAM attribution and a combined in-process chin bench should each come before any live-fps claim.

issues.problem: No live measurement supports 0.95. The best live/implied ratio ever observed is 0.80–0.85 (3090). On the RTX 6000 Ada the live plateau equalled the serial GPU turn. Today's ratio is 0.53–0.56. The plan's own §3 table gives P2 an efficiency of 0.88/0.93/0.97 and delivered 273/314/346. §5 rows 3a–4 then raise it to 0.92/0.95/0.98 without explanation. Adding chin, which means more GIL load in the same process, cannot raise efficiency unless P4 is done. C_chin15 measured CPU-chain lateness in a harness with only threads. It measured nothing about how well the GPU is kept fed. The break-even efficiency, 0.89 at the 338 ceiling, is above every live ratio ever recorded.
issues.correction: Keep P1's band (≤0.93 expected, 0.88 low) through rows 3–4 unless P4 is done. Restate the verdict as "unproven": 287 fps at 0.85, 314 at 0.93, and 300 needs ≥0.89. Make a saturating post-P1 run the gate that must pass before any 300 claim: N ≥ 14, GPU-event timing, L1–L4 layers.

Stagewise VRAM and bindings. _TensorRtOnnxStage calls create_execution_context() per stage, so each block's context gets its own activation memory, and the class supports only single-input/single-output bindings. UNet blocks need multi-IO and shared device memory. Measure VRAM for all 11 contexts at bs16 in 2.2.

State ownership across the process split. The pose chosen at a media worker selects the generation avatar's latents in the GPU process, and the motion-bank crossfade (_apply_webrtc_pose_crossfade) needs session state. The IPC path and its latency are not designed, and the 5–8 day estimate for media workers looks optimistic.

A disk budget for each round's pre-encode dump. Raw BGR is 1.376 MB/frame, so 2 identities × 20 s × 20 fps is about 1.1 GB against 1.3 GB free. Encode straight to lossless video, or cap a /dev/shm staging area.

The existing scheduler already re-sequences composed batches per job (next_compose_sequence, hls_gpu_scheduler.py:1868-1897). Ordered actors are needed for tracker state and the one-frame lookahead, not for output order. The plan's rationale should be corrected so the design keeps the existing re-sequencing.

reviews.verdict: The plan covers most of what the user asked for. It explains the 160 fps figure correctly, lists closed levers, gives decisions and kill criteria, and handles the tracker/crop correction well. Under a completeness and user-constraint lens it still has gaps that would stop it from putting the required recipe live, or from proving "15 x 20 fps smooth". The biggest gaps: (1) no work item creates chin assets (source landmarks, refined masks) for production avatars; (2) the accepted recipe was rendered at 24 fps while live runs at 20 fps; (3) the SHA reference harness does not replay live turn and tracker semantics. The pass metric is also broken as written: the counters reset every turn, and prebuffer gaps make "aggregate fresh ≥297" ill-defined. Resource hygiene is only tagged on 3 items, even though builds, golden-SHA replays and phase-exit load tests all load 5–11 GB. In-RAM engine builds at startup threaten SHA and E1 gate reproducibility. The go/no-go bench may time a different artifact than the one shipped. The efficiency assumptions behind the "321 expected" verdict are internally inconsistent: efficiency rises when chin is added, and K1 at 0.85 sits below the 0.89 needed for 300. Most fixes are additions to the plan, not reversals. The verdict should be restated with consistent efficiencies.

issues.claim: §6.4 pass: Aggregate fresh ≥297 fps; fresh = Δframes_played − Δframes_duplicated polled each second (0.4); S1 chains back-to-back turns ≥5 min
issues.problem: start_live() zeroes frames_played, frames_duplicated, queue_underruns and strict_video_stalls on every turn, so per-second deltas break at each boundary. Each turn also opens with a prebuffer, during which idle frames play and frames_played does not advance, followed by a return-to-idle transition. With 3–24 s WAVs and a 0.5 s prebuffer, even infinite GPU capacity delivers about 95% of 300, so the criterion cannot be met as written. Conversely, if it is relaxed to within-turn freshness, idle gaps let a GPU below 300 fps catch up and pass. Nothing verifies that 15 streams were actually speaking throughout the window.
issues.correction: Make the harness handle counter resets (or add monotonic lifetime counters server-side). Define certification as: (a) scheduler-side generated speaking frames ≥297/s sustained over ≥180 s; (b) a per-second speaker count of 15 for ≥99% of the window, using long concatenated turns or pre-queued next turns so there is no idle gap; (c) within-turn fresh ≥99.5% and the interval criteria. Report prebuffer/idle time separately.

# MuseTalk on RTX 4070 SUPER: path to 300 fps (15 × 20 fps streams)

This is a plan only. Nothing was implemented, and nothing ran on the GPU while writing it.

This is the final edit, made after three adversarial reviews: gpu-arithmetic, serving-resources and completeness-constraints. I checked every review claim against the probe JSON, the code, or a read-only box check before applying it. The rejected claims are listed separately.

**Evidence tags**

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [M] | Workflow-1 probe measurement. Files are listed in §10. |
| [M-now] | Read-only box check made while planning on 2026-09-27: df, free, du, ps, lscpu, stat, nvidia-smi query, git status. |
| [D] | Repo or experiment doc, or a log. |
| [C file:line] | Read in the source code. |
| [I] | Inference, with the arithmetic shown. |

- **fps** means fresh generated frames per second, summed over all streams.
- **Required recipe** means TAESD decoder + MuseTalk native avatar encoder (prepared SD-VAE latents, no runtime cost [D chin_fps README:3,49]) + 100% chin alignment + refined seam + expressive H3 source.
- **Live efficiency e** means delivered fps ÷ GPU ceiling fps.

---

## 1. Verdict

**300 fps (15 × 20 fps, all speaking at once, full required recipe) is projected, not measured.**
- **Expected: about 311 fps delivered, range 265–338** [I, §5].
- The expected case clears 300 by about 4%. The low case misses.

**It depends on two things that nobody has measured:**
1. **The ONNX-parser stagewise FP16 UNet at bs16 must run at ≤2.51 ms/frame sustained.**
   - Projected: 2.32 / 2.40 / 2.67 ms [I, §3.1].
2. **Live in-process efficiency must reach ≥0.90 at saturation after Phase 1.**
   - Assumed: 0.88 / 0.93 / 0.97 [I].
   - Every live ratio on record is lower:
     - 0.53–0.56 today, and that run was contaminated [D/I];
     - 0.80–0.85 on the 3090, with the old serial path [D].

**What is measured and what is projected**

| Piece | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Shipping bs8 .ts UNet + runtime CUDA graph | 23.43 ms/bs8 = 2.93 ms/frame | [M p6]. A 60-batch power-capped burst (~1.5 s), not a ≥60 s run |
| torch_tensorrt native bs16 + graph | 44.63 ms/bs16 = 2.79 ms/frame | [M ttrt_bs16]. Two rounds of 30 calls |
| ONNX-parser FP16, 11 per-block engines, bs8 | 20.575 ms sum = 2.57 ms/frame | [M]. Each block was timed alone with a sync per call; the blocks were never chained and never run sustained |
| bs16 factor for the ONNX path | 0.95 (0.92–1.0) | [I] from 5 micro-blocks. 3 of the 10 micro-runs had your server (pid 3305906) resident on the GPU [M gpu_log] |
| Full-height TRT TAESD | 0.486 ms/frame, FP16 NCHW output | [M p5]. The uint8 BGR output that item 2.1 ships was never built at full height, so 0.50–0.55 [I] |
| Other GPU (H2D + Whisper) | 0.08 (0.05–0.10) ms/frame | [D: H2D ~0.5 ms/bs8, docs/musetalk_4070s_pipeline_component_analysis_2026-09-22.md:80; M: Whisper 0.02] |
| Live efficiency after P1 | 0.88 / 0.93 / 0.97 | [I]. The top value is the offline pipelined harness, 250.8 / 258.7 = 0.97 [D/M] |
| Chin CPU chain, 15 streams in one process | 0 late frames | [M C_chin15]. Threads only; chin was a lighter stand-in; no GPU feeder, no asyncio or aiortc |

**Closest-to-measured stack** (torch_tensorrt bs16 + graph, full-height TRT TAESD):
- 2.79 + 0.51 + 0.08 = 3.38 ms → 296 fps ceiling → 256–291 delivered [I].
- It misses 300 at any efficiency.

**Lower-risk intermediate** (ONNX stagewise at bs8 + graph, item 2.3a):
- 2.53 + 0.51 + 0.08 = 3.12 ms → 321 ceiling → 298 expected (265–316) [I].
- The bs8 per-block sum is the most directly measured part of the ONNX gain.

**The single measurement that most changes the conclusion is item 2.2.**
- **What it is:** the 11 FP16 per-block engines chained exactly as the shipping stagewise backend, at bs16 and bs8, timed for ≥60 s at the power cap on a quiet box.
- **Why it decides:** it moves the GPU ceiling anywhere between 291 and 349 fps [I, §5].
  - ≤2.51 ms: lossless 300 is physically available, and the rest is serving engineering.
  - >2.64 ms: lossless 300 is gone, however good the serving path gets (K2).
- **Cost:** no backend code, and about one build-and-bench session.
- **Second most important:** the saturated in-process efficiency at the Phase 1 exit. It decides whether Phase 4 (the process split) is needed for 300.

**Go threshold for item 2.2** [I: UNet_max = 1000·e/300 − (0.51 TAESD + 0.08 other)]

| Live efficiency e | 0.85 | 0.88 | 0.90 | 0.93 | 0.95 | 0.97 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Max UNet ms/frame for 300 fps | 2.24 | 2.34 | 2.41 | 2.51 | 2.58 | 2.64 |

- **Go:** ≤2.51 ms, which gives lossless 300 at the expected efficiency.
- **Marginal:** 2.51–2.64 ms. This needs a measured e ≥0.95, or a lossy backstop (6.1 or 6.2).
- **No-go (K2):** >2.64 ms.
- The Phase 2 exit, K2 and item 2.2 all use this same rule, fed with the measured Phase 1 efficiency.

**Odds** [I, judgment, not computed]:
- Lossless 300 is roughly a coin flip on today's evidence.
- Both deciding quantities sit inside their projected ranges, but neither has been measured. The efficiency needed (0.90) is above every live ratio on record.
- The lossy backstops add margin only if they pass your video review. Their pass rates are unknown; for PTQ-only INT8 the rate is likely low (see 400 below).

**If the product is independent conversations rather than a wall:**
- 15 sessions at 50% speaking duty need 240 fps at p99. 20 sessions at 50% duty need 300 fps [I, binomial, §5].
- About 264 fps is expected after P1 + TRT TAESD, with no UNet rebuild [I: 2.93 + 0.51 + 0.08 = 3.52 ms → 284 × 0.93]. That serves 17 sessions at 50% duty (p99) [I].

**400 fps (20 × 20, all speaking): not reachable losslessly. The lossy paths need INT8 quality that does not exist yet.**
- **Best lossless:** 311 expected, 338 in the high case [I].
- **Mixed-INT8 UNet alone** (recipe v1, up0 and up1 kept in FP16) plus full-height FP16 TAESD: 2.49 ms → **373 expected**, short of 400 [I].
- **400 needs mixed-INT8 plus a second lossy lever:**
  - with INT8 TAESD at full height: 424 expected (357–465);
  - with tracker-row fill and the staged crop: 397 (335–434), just short [I].
- **INT8 quality today** [M quant_accuracy.json]:
  - The probe used 64 frames of one avatar, calibrated on the same avatar and decoded with SD-VAE, not TAESD.
  - On the rows the blend uses, naive INT8 gives 40.3 dB mean / 37.3 dB min, against a proposed gate of ≥45 / ≥42.
  - SmoothQuant made those rows worse: 39.9 / 35.9 dB.
  - The best PTQ variant (conv-only) reaches 6.09% latent rel-L2 and 41.1 / 38.3 dB on used rows.
  - Recipe v1's own error has never been measured. QAT or distillation is the realistic path.
- **It also needs Phase 4 (the process split)** [M D/F/G]:
  - 20 streams in one process with PyAV conversion: 19 late frames.
  - Same with cv2 conversion: 0 late frames, but p99 work was 49.5 ms against a 50 ms frame period.
  - 4 processes × 5 streams: 0 late frames at 12.6–23.8 ms.

**Binding ceilings, in the order they bind as each one is removed:**
1. **The serial single-process serving path (binds today).**
   - The scheduler does 3 syncs per batch plus a blocking D2H, and the handoff blocks it for 8–10 ms per 31.5–36 ms batch. That gives a structural ceiling of 174–203 fps [I: 8/(0.036+0.010); 8/(0.0315+0.008)].
   - Idle mp4 decode runs on the event loop. The loop saturates at 180–186 fps of total output, while a pre-decoded cache delivered 299.7 fps at 15 streams and 399.7 at 20 [M serving].
2. **UNet GPU time under the 220 W cap.**
   - After P2 the UNet is 2.40 of 2.99 ms per frame, 80% [I].
   - Power limit = maximum limit = 220 W [M-now]. SM clock under load is 2505–2625 MHz [M].
   - FP8 is a dead end on this card [M].
3. **The per-process GIL once chin runs live.**
   - The chin chain tops out at 567–665 fps per process [M U_ceiling_*].
   - The only 15-stream evidence (0 late; 34 ms mean / 40 ms p99 per 50 ms period) comes from a threads-only load.
     - Its chin stand-in cost about +1.5 ms, against 3.7–5.1 core-ms of refined chin beyond FaceMesh as written [M/D].
     - Per-frame work still inflated 4.5× versus one stream (7.58 → 34.1 ms) [M].
   - **Phase 4 is probable for 300 with chin live.** Item 3.0c decides.
4. **Host RAM (30 GB, shared).**
   - MemAvailable is 12.0 GB right now, with no MuseTalk server running. /dev/shm holds 8.9 GB, and Pylance has 4.4 GB RSS [M-now].
   - The in-process budget for 15 sessions is 9–14.5 GB [I, §3]. Adding the 4 GB guard, it does not fit, so **D2 is a hard prerequisite for any 15-stream work**.
   - The server has a 10.5 GB startup transient [D]. The cgroup oom_kill counter reads 12 [M-now].
5. **Disk:** 1.3 GB free [M-now] against 2.21 GB per .ts engine [M].
6. **NVENC:** capped at 12 sessions, using 2.47 GB of VRAM at 12 [M]. Encoding stays on the CPU with VP8.

**CPU is not binding in aggregate, but it has less headroom than the logical-CPU count suggests.**
- **Measured:** 10.6 logical CPUs busy at 300 fps [M C_chin15]; 12.1–13.1 at 400 [M D/F/G].
- **Added:** 0.5–3 for GPU feeding and aiortc [I].
- **Total:** 11–14 at 300 fps, 13–16 at 400.
- **Physical cores:** the 32 CPUs are SMT siblings on 16 cores; CPU n and CPU n+16 share core n [M-now lscpu].
  - Against about 20 core-equivalents [I: 16 × ~1.25], that is 55–70% at 300 and 65–80% at 400.
  - Contention already shows: FaceMesh CPU per frame rose from 3.4 to 13.2 ms under the C_chin15 load [M results_fm.jsonl; fm_during_C_chin15.json].

**Corrections to the evidence digest.** All were verified in files. The first one changes the verdict.
1. **The staged exact-crop TAESD (0.345 ms) is not usable with the required chin recipe.**
   - The tracker pastes the whole raw 256×256 generated face into the frame before FaceMesh sees it [C experiments/chin_fps_validation_20260927/run.py:38-41, called at :139; same in h3_avatar_workflow/backend.py Tracker].
   - Rows above R therefore change the landmarks and so the chin warp. The p7 row scan covered only the blend mask [M].
   - So the recipe needs full-height TAESD. The digest's "304.6 fps measured GPU path" becomes about **284 fps** for this recipe [I: 23.43/8 + 0.51 + 0.08 = 3.52 ms].
   - The crop comes back only as lossy item 6.1.
2. **CUDA-graph mode does not free the feeder core.**
   - `graph_no_spinner` still burns 23.5 ms of CPU per bs8 call [M gil.json].
   - The probe issues calls back to back with no per-call sync [C unet_probe/probe_gil.py:61-67], so this is launch-queue back-pressure, not a sync spin.
   - A blocking event (item 1.3) recovers the core only if depth-2 pipelining bounds the work in flight. Measure feeder CPU per batch in the real loop.
3. **ONNX-path bs16 factor and clocks.**

### 3.1 How the UNet estimates were built, and what must not be stacked

- Start: 20.575 ms per bs8, the sum of 11 per-block engines [M], so 2.572 ms per frame.
- Multiply by, for low / expected / high:
  - **bs16 factor:** 0.92 / 0.95 / 1.0.
    - 0.92 is the torch_tensorrt whole-UNet ratio 45.34/49.29 [M].
    - 0.95 is about the ONNX micro-block mean of 0.942 [I], rounded up because torch_tensorrt micro-blocks (mean 0.931) under-predicted their own whole-UNet ratio (0.920) [M].
    - 1.0 means no gain.
  - **CUDA graph:** 0.98 / 0.984 / 0.995 [M: 44.63/45.34 at bs16; raw TRT at bs8 23.62/24.04 = 0.9825].
  - **Sum-of-blocks:** 1.0. The stagewise backend keeps the block boundaries (§1, correction 3).
  - **Clock:** 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.044, half of 2790/2565 [I].
- **Result: 2.32 / 2.40 / 2.67 ms** [I].
- The worst stacked case (full clock penalty and no bs16 gain) is 2.78 ms, equal to the fallback. That is K2.

**ONNX stagewise at bs8** (item 2.3a): 2.572 × 0.98 / 0.9825 / (0.995 × 1.044) = **2.52 / 2.53 / 2.67 ms** [I].

**Mixed-INT8 recipe v1.** INT8 in down0–3, mid, up2 and up3; FP16 in up0, up1, head and tail.
- Per bs8: 16.30 ms [I from M per-block: the INT8 sum of 14.36, with the INT8 up0/up1/tail times swapped for their FP16 times].
- Per frame: 2.04 ms, times the same factors → **1.84 / 1.91 / 2.12 ms**; worst case 2.21 [I].
- A lossier recipe that also puts up0 in INT8 (7.2% block error) would be 15.82 ms per bs8 [I: 14.36 − 2.23 + 3.69], or 1.78 ms per frame optimistic. That is not v1.

**TAESD, full height, uint8 output: 0.50 / 0.51 / 0.55 ms** [I].

- The crop's in-pipeline overhead was 0.346 → 0.354 ms, about +2% [M p5/p6].

**Other: 0.05 / 0.08 / 0.10 ms** [D/M]. The low end assumes H2D overlaps on a copy stream, which no item does yet.

**Overlaps that must not be stacked:**
- **CUDA graph gain at bs16** is −1.6% (45.34 → 44.63 ms [M]), not the bs8 figure.
- **Idle-gap fixes** all close the same idle gap: turning syncs off, double buffering, the non-blocking handoff and the idle cache. Together they are capped at an efficiency of about 0.97 [D offline harness].

- **Clock penalty and thermal soak** are one mechanism. Only the clock term is counted.
- **Demand reductions** (skipping discarded GPU work, speaking duty cycle) reduce the frames needed, not the cost per frame. They are kept out of the waterfall.

**Invariants**
1. One thread issues UNet and TAESD work. Whisper is the one exception: it runs on its own stream in the prep thread. All graphs are captured at warmup, or with `capture_error_mode='thread_local'`.
2. The GPU process never waits on a media process. Backpressure comes from ring occupancy, read at selection time.
3. Per-stream order is kept end to end.
4. Pixel math, including the tracker-input paste, runs on NumPy 1.23.5 and OpenCV 4.9.
5. Run-ahead is stored as faces: 23.5 MB per stream for 6 s, vs 83 MB as I420 [I]. Compose happens at most 1.5 s ahead.
6. Idle playback never decodes and never touches the GPU.
7. Every stage sits behind a flag, and 0 restores the in-process path.
8. Session state that selects GPU work (pose, motion bank) lives in the GPU process. Media workers send pose and barge-in commands over the control socket.

## 6. Validation protocol

### 6.1 Box conditions (every stage)
- `box_guard.sh` passes before and after each stage. D2 is resolved.
- Only the candidate server runs on the GPU, inside an approved lease window, with your live server stopped.
- No SoulX or Codex GPU processes. The GPU sits at 0% for 10 s before each stage.
- MemAvailable ≥4 GB throughout; oom_kill unchanged; test disk writes within the ledger.
- `ps` and `nvidia-smi` snapshots every 10 s. The run is **contaminated** if a foreign GPU process appears or foreign CPU exceeds 1 core; repeat it.

### 6.2 Rig
- **Audio:** the item 0.5 corpus, distinct per session, with `MUSETALK_DISABLE_LOCAL_TTS=1`.
  - S1 uses concatenated long turns or `--chain`, so every stream speaks for the whole window.
- **Content:** the required recipe on H3 expressive sources.
  - At least 3 certification identities, each with chin assets (3.0a) and your chin acceptance (D20).
  - chinese_bob is included only after that acceptance.
  - 5 sessions per identity.
- **Client:**
  - Off-box if possible (D16).
  - On-box: pin by **physical core**. The client gets cores 12–15 = CPUs {12–15, 28–31}; the server gets {0–11, 16–27} [M-now lscpu: CPU n+16 shares core n].
  - Shard at ≤5 peers per client process.
  - The run is invalid if client loop-lag p99 exceeds 20 ms.
  - On-box loopback receivers showed p99 gaps of 62–108 ms even at light load [M], so cadence is judged on server-side send timestamps as well as the client.
- **Certification is loopback / LAN only.** The real-network run is reported separately (D21).

| S0 | Smoke test, N = 1 and 3. It also produces the round's video. | – |

### 6.4 Metrics, pass criteria and quality gates

**Metrics.**
- **Per stream, per second** (lifetime monotonic counters, item 0.4):
  - fresh = Δframes_played; held = Δframes_duplicated; stall = Δstrict_video_stall_seconds;
  - queue_underruns; run-ahead seconds;

**Pass criteria for "300 fps / 15 streams certified"** (S1 at N = 15, 3 of 3 repeats, ≥180 s of steady state):
- **Throughput:**
  - Scheduler-side generated speaking frames ≥297 per second, sustained.

  - output_fps = 20 asserted.
- **Per stream, within turns:**
  - fresh ≥99.5% of output slots after the prebuffer; no held run longer than 2 frames;
  - 0 stall seconds; 0 underruns after the prebuffer;
  - average interval 0.050 ± 0.001 s; maximum ≤0.100 s on server send timestamps;

Stacking both would double-count, so the high case's half-clock term (x1.044) covers both, and the >=5 min runs in 0.8 and >=60 s runs in 2.2 settle it.

The micro-block re-measure is left as an implicit fallback only if the chain cannot be built.

residual_uncertainties: Chained stagewise FP16 UNet at bs16 under sustained power-capped load: projected 2.32/2.40/2.67 ms, worst 2.78. This single number decides whether lossless 300 is physically possible (go at 2.51 ms or less, K2 above 2.64). Nothing but isolated per-block bursts has been measured.

Saturated live in-process efficiency after Phase 1: assumed 0.88-0.97. The only live data is 0.53-0.56 (contaminated) and the historical 0.80-0.85 (old serial path), and 300 needs about 0.90 or more at the expected 334 ceiling.

Whether live chin fits in one process at 15 streams (GIL). The only evidence is a threads-only synthetic with a +1.5 ms chin stand-in, which already shows 4.5x per-frame inflation. Item 3.0c decides whether Phase 4 (another 12-17 days) is required for 300.

Host RAM: the 15-session in-process footprint is estimated at 9-14.5 GB against 12.0 GB available today. Every decisive measurement (0.8, 0.9, 2.2, load tests) depends on the user freeing /dev/shm (D2).

Whether TRT TAESD (about 2 LSB) and the stagewise UNet pass G-TRACK with a stateful FaceMesh tracker, and whether the user counts them as no-quality-change (D14). A K3 failure alone drops the expected case to about 279 fps.

The recipe is not yet defined for live 20 fps: production avatars lack chin assets (3.0a), and the accepted chin recipe was reviewed at 24 fps (0.10, D18). Chin acceptance for chinese_bob and any new H3 identity is still pending.
All GPU ms come from 1.5-2 s bursts. Sustained clock and thermal behaviour at the 220 W cap over minutes is unmeasured, and full-height uint8 TAESD (0.50-0.55 ms) was never built.

INT8 quality for 400 fps: naive INT8 is about 5 dB short on used rows. Recipe v1's error is unmeasured, the probe used one avatar decoded with SD-VAE, and QAT is probably required. 400 also needs a second lossy lever and Phase 4.
